rows.description: A student receives help and slowly feels obliged and watched. Gifts that carry hidden expectation create discomfort, while clean gifts allow the receiver to keep dignity.
graph_context: this subtopic also appears at ages: 4–6, 7–12, 23–26

rows.description: A person who accepts help with a simple thank you, without excessive apology or self-belittling, lets the giver feel useful. Receiving is also a form of generosity.
graph_context: this subtopic also appears at ages: 4–6, 7–12, 18–22

rows.description: A young earner supports family and friends but sets a sustainable boundary so that giving does not become resentment or ruin. Sustainable generosity includes the giver's own needs.
graph_context: this subtopic also appears at ages: 4–6, 7–12, 18–22

rows.description: A teenager everyone turns to for notes, comfort and favours starts feeling drained and quietly resentful. Being the reliable one becomes a role that is hard to step out of.
graph_context: this subtopic also appears at ages: 18–22, 23–26

rows.description: A student who has been listening to friends' problems all week feels selfish declining another call. Guilt often signals a long habit of over-giving, not actual wrongdoing.
graph_context: this subtopic also appears at ages: 13–17, 23–26

rows.description: A daughter or eldest son who is expected to sacrifice for everyone feels unseen when tired. Cultural duty can be sincere and still cost more than one person can pay.
graph_context: this subtopic also appears at ages: 13–17, 18–22

rows.description: A friend sees a usual giver becoming curt and withdrawn and offers to help them for a change. Caring for the carer is often overlooked until they break.
graph_context: this subtopic also appears at ages: 13–17, 18–22

rows.description: A person who gives a lot schedules rest, shares the load and says a clear no to some requests. Keeping kindness sustainable protects both the giver and those depending on them.
graph_context: this subtopic also appears at ages: 13–17, 18–22

rows.description: A child asks why people die, why they are here and what happens next. These questions are early meaning-making, and honest simple answers respect them better than deflection.
graph_context: this subtopic also appears at ages: 13–17, 18–22, 23–26

rows.description: A teenager experiments with causes, faiths, aesthetics and friend groups, trying to find what feels worth living for. The search looks chaotic from outside but is serious work inside.
graph_context: this subtopic also appears at ages: 7–12, 18–22, 23–26
